standard.title: Prendre / Apprendre / Comprendre (Irregular Verbs — Prendre Family)
standard.explanation: Prendre (to take) is an irregular verb. Conjugation: je prends, tu prends, il/elle/on prend, nous prenons, vous prenez, ils/elles prennent. Notice the double 'n' in the ils/elles form. Two important compounds follow the same pattern: apprendre (to learn) — j'apprends, tu apprends, il apprend, nous apprenons, vous apprenez, ils apprennent; and comprendre (to understand) — je comprends, tu comprends, il comprend, nous comprenons, vous comprenez, ils comprennent. All three verbs use the same irregular stem changes.

examples.english: I'm taking a coffee. / I'm having a coffee.
They are taking the firefighter's help.

drills.question: Quel est le verbe conjugué au présent: 'Je ___ la situation'?
drills.explanation: Avec 'je', le verbe prendre se conjugue en 'je prends' (avec un 'd' à la fin).

drills.question: Tu ___ le français? (apprendre)
drills.explanation: Avec 'tu', apprendre devient 'tu apprends' (double n dans cette forme).

drills.question: Nous ___ l'aide. (comprendre)
drills.explanation: Avec 'nous', comprendre devient 'nous comprenons' (pas de changement au radical).

drills.question: Ils ___ leur situation. (prendre)
drills.explanation: Avec 'ils', prendre devient 'ils prennent' (double 'n' avant le 'e').

drills.question: Vous ___ le français? (apprendre)
drills.explanation: Avec 'vous', apprendre devient 'vous apprenez' (ez à la fin).

advanced.title: Prendre / Apprendre / Comprendre — Full Conjugation, Compounds & Expressions
advanced.explanation: The prendre family includes several important verbs with the same irregular pattern. Prendre (to take), apprendre (to learn), and comprendre (to understand) all follow: je prends, tu prends, il/elle/on prend, nous prenons, vous prenez, ils/elles prennent. Additional compounds: reprendre (to take back, resume), surprendre (to surprise), and entreprendre (to undertake) use identical conjugations. Common expressions with prendre include: prendre du temps (to take time), prendre un café (to have a coffee), prendre en charge (to take care of/responsibility for), prendre feu (to catch fire — used metaphorically and literally), prendre conscience (to become aware). These expressions are idiomatic and must be learned as phrases.

standard.scenario: You are calling emergency services. Report an accident you have witnessed and describe what happened. Be clear, stay calm, and provide key details like location and the number of vehicles involved.
standard.modelAnswer: Allô, c'est une urgence! Il y a un accident près de la gare. Deux voitures se sont heurtées. Une personne est blessée. Les pompiers peuvent arriver?
standard.modelAnswerExplanation: The answer includes: 1) Recognition of the emergency, 2) Location of the accident, 3) Number of vehicles involved, 4) Number of injured, 5) Request for help. All phrases use simple present or passé composé appropriate for A1 level.
standard.tip: Speak clearly and calmly. Provide specific location details (near the station, on the main road, etc.). Always mention if there are injured people so dispatchers know to send an ambulance.

advanced.scenario: You are calling the emergency dispatch line to report a serious accident. Explain the situation in detail: what happened, how many people are injured, the severity of injuries, the exact location, and any additional hazards or complications. Use the prendre family verbs and full sentences.
keyPhrases: Il y a eu un accident grave.
Je prends en charge la situation.
advanced.modelAnswer: Allô, c'est une urgence grave! Un accident s'est produit sur la route nationale à trois kilomètres de la gare. Je comprends qu'il y a deux voitures impliquées. Trois personnes sont blessées, et l'une d'elles saigne abondamment. Je prends en charge la scène et je garde les témoins en sécurité. Pouvez-vous appeler l'ambulance immédiatement?
advanced.modelAnswerExplanation: The answer demonstrates: 1) Clear emergency declaration, 2) Precise location with distance reference, 3) Number of vehicles involved, 4) Detailed injury information with severity assessment, 5) Responsible action (taking charge of the scene), 6) Polite request for ambulance. Uses prendre en charge (to take responsibility), comprendre (to understand), and appeler (to call).
advanced.tip: Use 'prendre en charge' to show you are managing the situation responsibly. Provide specific medical details (saignement = bleeding, inconscient = unconscious, etc.). Use full sentences with connectors like 'et' and 'mais' for clarity. Stay composed and speak at a measured pace.
